PullRequest.Title: sessions: pin chat canvases to the Agents window sidebar
PullRequest.Body:
## TL;DR In the Agents window, a user can now **pin a chat's canvas to the sidebar**. A pinned canvas stays live while the user works in other chats, and clicking its sidebar row shows it on a full page of its own, without switching to its chat. The canvas stays owned by its chat, whose agent keeps updating it. No issue was filed. The series is rebased on `main` (`3ee7c48cab0`), is split into 11 commits that each build and pass tests, and is meant to be reviewed commit by commit (see the [review guide](#review-guide-commit-by-commit)). ## Background (no prior context needed) - **Canvas:** a live web page that a chat's agent opens and keeps updating, such as a plan, a preview, or a dashboard. It is served by a canvas extension that runs in the agent host, and the window renders it in a native web contents view. Each canvas is owned by one chat: `ICanvasOwner = { providerId, session, chat }`. - **How canvases are shown today:** `CanvasService` (`vs/workbench/contrib/canvases`) shows a canvas only while its owning chat is visible, as an editor tab beside that chat (`isOwnerPresentable`). In the Agents window, `SessionCanvasContextService` reports only the active session's active chat as visible, and the Agent Host provider subscribes to a chat's canvases only while its session is active. - **The problem:** as soon as the user switches chats, a canvas disappears, and its updates are no longer observed. Users want to keep a canvas at hand, for example a plan they check between turns. - **Why it can stay live:** holding a subscription to a canvas channel keeps the owning agent-host session resident. A pinned canvas only needs the client to keep that subscription; no host or protocol change is needed. ## What changes for users All of this is gated on `ChatContextKeys.enabled`, the Agents window (not auxiliary windows), and `chat.canvases.enabled`. - **Pinning:** - An **Add to Sidebar / Remove from Sidebar** toggle (pin / unpin icons) in the title of an active canvas editor. - The same choice in a canvas tab's context menu. - **Agents: Add Canvas to Sidebar...** in the Command Palette, which picks among the shown chat's live canvases. - It is deliberately not labeled "Pin", which would clash with Pin Tab and the sessions **Pinned** section. - **Sidebar rows:** - Placement: in the default layout, pinned canvases are rows directly below **Automations**. With `sessions.sidebar.separateNavigation`, they come last in the navigation shortcuts. There are no rows when nothing is pinned. - Content: each row shows the canvas title, its chat as secondary text, and its state (live, not connected, or unavailable), and is highlighted while its page is shown. - Actions: hovering or keyboard focus reveals a **Remove from Sidebar** button. The context menu offers **Go to Chat**, **Remove from Sidebar** and **Close Canvas**. - **Canvas page:** - Clicking a row shows the canvas full-page, replacing the sessions grid like Automations does. It never switches to the owning chat. - Its icon-only header offers the same three actions. - Back/Forward return to the canvas each opening showed. - **Lifecycle:** - Up to 5 pins, with a notification when full. - Pins persist per workspace and reconnect after a reload. - A pin is removed automatically when its session or chat is deleted or archived, or when its canvas is closed through Close Canvas (from the page, the row, or the chat). - Closing a canvas's editor tab does not unpin it. - A pin whose canvas is gone shows as unavailable with **Remove from Sidebar**. ## How it works ```mermaid flowchart TB subgraph WB["vs/workbench/contrib/canvases (shared)"] CE["CanvasEditor (editor tab)"] --> CV["CanvasView"] CV --> CS["CanvasService
isOwnerPresentable: may open as an editor
isPresentable: may attach in a view"] CS --> CCS["ICanvasContextService
+ optional getTrackedCanvas, isCanvasTracked, isPresentedElsewhere"] end subgraph SW["vs/sessions (Agents window)"] PAGE["Canvas page (custom view)"] --> CV PAGE --> PCS["IPinnedCanvasService
pins, storage, lifecycle"] ROWS["Sidebar rows and actions"] --> PCS SCCS["SessionCanvasContextService"] -. implements .-> CCS SCCS --> PCS PCS --> SMS["ISessionsManagementService
observeCanvas, observeChatCanvases"] SMS --> PROV["ISessionsProvider optional hooks
Agent Host: no active-session gate"] end ``` - **Shared canvas layer (`vs/workbench/contrib/canvases`):** - The rendering moves out of `CanvasEditor` into a reusable `CanvasView`. - `ICanvasService` gains `isPresentable`, separate from `isOwnerPresentable`. - `ICanvasContextService` gains three optional members, so a host can keep canvases live outside their owner's visibility without ever opening them as editors. - **Provider-neutral liveness (`vs/sessions`):** two optional `ISessionsProvider` hooks, `observeCanvas` and `observeChatCanvases`, are routed through `ISessionsManagementService`. Shared sessions code never imports provider code. The Agent Host provider implements them without the active-session gate. - **Pins:** - `IPinnedCanvasService` keeps pins and their storage, and holds one `observeCanvas` reference per pin. - `SessionCanvasContextService` reports pins to `CanvasService`. - The page is a custom view (`sessions.customView.canvas`). A custom view opening can now carry a `state` (the pin) for history. - **Specs:** `SESSIONS.md` (the pin contract), `SESSIONS_LIST.md` (row placement and ownership) and `LAYOUT.md` (custom view history state) are updated concisely. ## Key decisions | Decision | Why | |---|---| | A pinned canvas stays owned by its chat | Its agent keeps driving it. Pinning only keeps it live and gives it a second place to be shown. | | `isPresentable` is separate from `isOwnerPresentable` | Editors keep their current rule (beside the visible owner only), so a pinned canvas can never auto-open as an editor in another chat's working set. Only views, such as the page, use the wider rule. | | Persist identity only (provider, session, chat, extension, canvas type, instance ID, last title), never the URL | Canvas URLs carry access tokens and change whenever the canvas restarts. A pin rebinds to the live canvas with the same instance ID. | | Clicking a pin always shows its page, never its chat | It keeps the user where they are. A pin that isn't connected after a reload reconnects through `observeChatCanvases` without showing the chat. | | One browser model per canvas, attached to one view at a time | The same canvas can be in an editor and on the page. A hidden view never takes the model from a visible one, and takes it back once it is visible again. | | At most 5 pins | Each pin keeps its session resident in the agent host. | ## Review guide (commit by commit) Each commit builds and passes the affected test suites on its own. | # | Commit | What to review | Size | |---|---|---|---| | 1 | `canvases: extract CanvasView from CanvasEditor` | Mostly moved code. New logic: one view at a time owns a browser model (claim, yield, reclaim). It also includes main's corner-radius forwarding (#344727), which moved into `CanvasView._measure` during the rebase. | +667 / −383 | | 2 | `canvases: let other surfaces track and present a canvas` | `isPresentable` versus `isOwnerPresentable`. External presentations: their models are retained and then released. Closing a tab while the page shows its canvas keeps the model. A request ahead of reconciliation waits for the update to settle. | +130 / −23 | | 3 | `sessions: observe chat canvases outside the active session` | The optional provider hooks, routing through the management service, the Agent Host implementation, and `onDidCloseCanvas`. | +178 / −5 | | 4 | `sessions: return custom views to the item each opening showed` | Custom view `state` and `acceptsState`, and Back/Forward history. | +102 / −13 | | 5 | `sessions: add a service for canvases pinned to the sidebar` | `IPinnedCanvasService`: storage (identity only), the cap, rebinding after a reload, and automatic removal. Most of the size is tests. | +1317 | | 6 | `sessions: present pinned canvases outside their chat` | `SessionCanvasContextService` wiring. A pinned canvas is presentable only on the page, never as an editor in another chat. | +194 / −5 | | 7 | `sessions: add a full-page view for pinned canvases` | The canvas page custom view and its states (live, reconnecting, unavailable). | +206 | | 8 | `sessions: add actions to pin canvases to the sidebar` | Actions, menus, context keys and gating. | +422 | | 9 | `sessions: list pinned canvases in the sidebar` | Rows in both sidebar layouts, accessibility labels, the hover toolbar, and the context menu. | +426 / −8 | | 10 | `canvases: hold the last frame while a canvas view switches canvases` | Polish: no empty flash when switching pins. `WebContentsViewHost.setVisible(visible, immediate)`. | +232 / −7 | | 11 | `sessions: keep shortcut rows highlighted without a pointer focus ring` | Polish: no stale focus outline under pointer focus, and the active row keeps its highlight. | +111 / −2 | ## Review so far An automated AI review of the full series (GPT-6 Astra; architecture, decisions, correctness, security, engineering, implementation) judged the architecture sound. It reported 4 high and 2 medium findings, and all are fixed in the commits above. Each fix has a regression test that fails without it. | Finding | Fix | In commit | |---|---|---| | High: the canvas page could stay on "Loading canvas…" after a canvas restarted with a new URL | Model resolution lets the update settle before judging the source | 2 | | High: closing a canvas tab while its page showed it reloaded the page and leaked the new model | The editor input is released first, and the presentation is kept as external while the page shows it | 2 | | High: Close Canvas from the chat left an "Unavailable" pin | Close events match the last canvas the pin was bound to | 5 | | High: deleting a session from another client left its pins | Sessions reported as `removed` drop their pins (catalog-hidden sessions report no removal) | 5 | | Medium: pins of owners archived while the window was closed stayed | Archived owners are pruned on load and on every catalog change | 5 | | Medium: a slow close could unpin a reopened canvas | Only the close event of the bound canvas removes a pin | 5 | ## Interactions with `main` and other PRs - **Rebase onto `main`:** - On `main`, `SessionCanvasContextService.isOwnerVisible` is false while any custom view is open. The canvas page is a custom view, so a pinned canvas is admitted there only through `isPresentedElsewhere`. The pinned-canvas tests now open the page as a custom view. - Main's Inbox sidebar row is kept, and pins still follow Automations. - **#345093 (draft):** - It also changes `CanvasEditor`'s load state machine and `CanvasService`'s source handling (it keeps the view while a provider reconnects). - This PR moves that `CanvasEditor` logic into `CanvasView`, so whichever lands second must port the other's changes. - **#345102:** it also touches `canvasService.ts`. ## Out of scope / follow-ups - **Chat-input pill:** a pin entry in the chat-input canvases pill (`IChatPillEntry` has only one promoted action). - **Agent host restarts:** by host design, canvases are not restored after an agent host *process* restart (`AGENT_HOST_SESSIONS_PROVIDER.md`), so pins then show as unavailable. A follow-up could reopen the instance with the pin's stored identity. - **Residency cost:** each pin keeps its session resident. The cap bounds this. - **Validation gaps:** - **Agents: Add Canvas to Sidebar...** has no automated test and was not exercised manually. - Two unit tests are still missing: - resolving a pinned canvas through the tracked-canvas fallback for another session with unknown membership; - releasing bound pin subscriptions when canvases or AI are disabled, on service disposal, and on provider reconnection. ## How to test 1. Set `"chat.canvases.enabled": true` and open the Agents window. Start a Copilot CLI session and ask the agent to open a canvas. 2. In the canvas editor's title, select **Add to Sidebar** (pin icon). A row appears below **Automations**, showing the canvas title, the chat, and the live state. 3. Switch to another chat or session, then select the row. The canvas shows full-page and live, without switching chats. Back returns. 4. Hover the row to see **Remove from Sidebar**. Right-click it for **Go to Chat**, **Remove from Sidebar** and **Close Canvas**. 5. Reload the window and select the row. It reconnects without showing its chat. 6. Close the canvas from the page or the chat: the row disappears. Archive or delete the chat: its rows disappear. Close only the editor tab: the row stays. 7. Pin a sixth canvas: a notification explains the limit of 5. 8. Toggle `"sessions.sidebar.separateNavigation"` to check the other sidebar layout. ## Validation All of the following ran on the rebased branch (`main` at `3ee7c48cab0`): | Command | Result | |---|---| | `npm run typecheck-client` | Passed | | `./scripts/test.sh --runGlob "vs/{sessions/contrib/canvases,workbench/contrib/canvases,workbench/contrib/browserView,sessions/contrib/sessions,sessions/services/sessions,sessions/services/customView,sessions/contrib/providers/agentHost}/test/**/*.test.js"` | 3297 passing, 19 pending, 0 failing | | Per commit: `tsc --noEmit -p src/tsconfig.json` and the same test glob, on each of the 11 commits | All passed (3263 to 3297 passing, 0 failing) | | `npm run eslint -- <40 changed .ts files>` | Passed | | `node build/hygiene.ts ` | Passed | | `npm run stylelint -- <3 changed .css files>` | Passed. Its 3 design-token suggestions are on lines this PR doesn't touch. | | `npm run valid-layers-check` | Passed | | `git diff --check` | Clean | The regression tests for the six review findings were also run against the unfixed sources, before the rebase. All six failed there and pass with the fixes. Manual testing in Code OSS, before the rebase, covered: - pinning from the editor title; - both sidebar layouts; - switching chats and opening pins from the sidebar; - the hover button and the context menu; - the page's icon-only header; - the held frame when switching pins; - the shortcut-row focus ring. It has not been repeated after the rebase yet.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The changed synchronous call path, O(screenshot bytes) implementation, full-viewport source, and pre-existing encoded placeholder are directly established in repository code. Exact milliseconds depend on viewport/image complexity, which is reflected in medium severity rather than uncertainty about the mechanism.
Findings.PerformanceResource: CPU work and image-sized JavaScript string allocations
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Each visible canvas input switch performs work linear in the compressed screenshot byte length; repeatedly selecting pinned canvases repeats the full encoding and allocates a new base64/data-URL string each time.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Increased click-to-display latency, UI-thread stalls, and GC pressure when switching high-resolution canvases
Findings.PreviousBehavior: CanvasEditor switched inputs by detaching the existing model directly; it did not synchronously serialize the model screenshot during setInput. WebContentsViewHost already encoded captured screenshots for its placeholder on the asynchronous capture path.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: CanvasView.setInput now calls holdFrame synchronously, and holdFrame passes the full viewport screenshot through encodeBase64 before the selected canvas can change.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: RIGHT line 234 newly invokes encodeBase64(screenshot) inside holdFrame; holdFrame is newly called synchronously from CanvasView.setInput on every visible input change.
Findings.Title: Reuse the prepared placeholder instead of re-encoding the frame
Findings.Impact: Clicking another pinned canvas, or switching a visible canvas editor input, blocks the renderer while encodeBase64 loops over the quality-80 full-viewport JPEG and builds a roughly 4/3-sized string. Large/high-DPI canvas frames or rapid sidebar switching can therefore produce noticeable input jank and allocation/GC spikes.
Findings.Evidence: PinnedCanvasPage's selected-entry autorun calls view.setInput directly (pinnedCanvasPage.ts:89), which calls holdFrame before updating the input (canvasView.ts:207-214). The added line serializes model.screenshot synchronously. BrowserViewModel.captureScreenshot stores a full-page capture in model.screenshot (browserView.ts:913-919), and encodeBase64 is a synchronous byte-by-byte loop with repeated string appends (buffer.ts:431-459). WebContentsViewHost already turns that same screenshot into its placeholder background (webContentsViewHost.ts:241-244), so this is duplicate serialization on the interaction path rather than unavoidable capture work.
Findings.Recommendation: Before detaching the host, reuse or transfer the already-prepared background image from host.screenshotElement (or retain an object URL/pre-encoded representation) for the held frame. Keep encoding/capture off the synchronous setInput path.

Scenarios.Scenario: Reload the Agents window with persisted pinned canvases
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Workspace storage parsing and pin/sidebar construction are synchronous. Agent-host canvas observations start after service construction but their asynchronous snapshots are not required for the sidebar rows to render; live state arrives later.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read and later write the small persisted pin identity list through IStorageService
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One read at service creation; writes on pin/unpin/selection/title changes, serializing at most 5 identities
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The initial read/JSON parse is on sidebar initialization; later writes follow explicit user or title changes.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Subscribe to each pinned canvas channel in the Agent Host
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most 5 distinct canvas subscriptions; duplicate resources are refcounted by AgentSubscriptionManager
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Inactive sessions had no pin-owned canvas subscriptions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Not required for initial row rendering; determines when pending rows become live.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Persisted pins, hard-capped at 5; effective channel cardinality is at most one distinct canvas resource per pin.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Up to 5 distinct canvas observations may be active. The client AgentSubscriptionManager refcounts identical resource channels, and the pin cap bounds aggregate residency.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Cold reload restores identity/title from workspace storage and initially has no live canvas binding. Warm provider state may immediately satisfy observations; otherwise entries remain pending. Negative/unknown membership is distinguished from authoritative empty membership.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: storage, cap, subscription creation, refcounting, and disposal paths are directly traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Agent-host session residency cost varies by provider/session, but the five-pin cap is explicit.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional finding: the new residency and startup work are intentional, bounded, asynchronous relative to initial row rendering, and released on disable/unpin/session removal/disposal.

Scenarios.Scenario: Pin, unpin, archive, delete, or close a canvas
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Pinning synchronously updates bounded observables/storage and starts one canvas observation. Closing awaits one provider close operation; unpin/archive/delete dispose the associated references and storage entry.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Observe or close one provider-owned canvas
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One observation when pinning and one close call when explicitly closing
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Canvas close existed, but pin-owned inactive-session observation and the close notification did not.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Observation is off the pin UI critical path; close completion is awaited before reporting closed.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Persist the bounded updated pin list
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One small write per explicit pin/unpin/selection change; at most 5 entries
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Synchronous service call after the in-memory state change.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One targeted canvas per action, with removal scans bounded by 5 pins.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One close request per explicit action; no changed burst scheduler. Canvas observations are independently held and capped.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Pin identity deduplicates by provider/session/chat/type/instance. Live observations are reused by resource in the agent-host subscription manager; missing sessions suspend observations until they return.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: all ownership and cleanup events are explicit and covered by changed tests.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Storage backend timing is platform-dependent, but payload size is strictly bounded.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: operation counts are constant/bounded, and subscriptions are disposed across unpin, disable, replacement, archive/delete, and service disposal.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open, reconnect, and switch pinned canvas pages
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A connected cold canvas must resolve/create a browser model and load its HTTP(S) source before display; a warm retained model is reused. A restored unresolved pin first observes chat membership. Before either path progresses, switching a visible CanvasView synchronously holds the previous frame.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Load the canvas HTTP(S) source in a native browser model
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One cold model load per viewed pinned canvas; warm switches reuse the retained model; at most 5 pinned models
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same operation existed for canvas editors, but pinned full-page views can now trigger it outside the owning chat.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cold load is on the display critical path; warm reuse avoids it.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Observe chat membership and its advertised canvas states to rebind a restored pin
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One chat channel plus one refcounted channel per currently advertised canvas while reconnecting
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Inactive chats were not observed for canvas reconnection.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The target canvas state must arrive before the restored pin can bind; observers are released after success or authoritative absence.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Synchronously base64-encode the previous full-viewport JPEG for a held frame
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Once per visible input switch, linear in screenshot bytes
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Input switching detached the model without this extra synchronous serialization; the host already prepared its own encoded placeholder asynchronously.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Directly blocks the selection/input path before the next canvas is set.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Canvas screenshot byte size and number of user switches drive the reported synchronous cost. Reconnect membership scales with open canvases in the owning chat; pins remain capped at 5.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Only the selected page attaches a browser model. Several quickly selected unresolved pins can hold membership observers, but identical Agent Host resources are refcounted; distinct canvas channels are subscribed concurrently by the existing chat-canvas projection.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Warm models are retained per pinned canvas and reused; cold models are created once viewed. Restored pins use persisted identity but not stale URL/resource, and temporary chat membership observation is released after match/authoritative miss.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high: setInput-to-holdFrame call flow and encodeBase64's byte loop are direct.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact frame size and encoding duration depend on viewport, DPI, and image complexity; this affects severity, not the established synchronous mechanism.
Scenarios.Verdict: One medium finding submitted for duplicate synchronous full-frame encoding. Cold browser/network work and temporary reconnect subscriptions otherwise follow bounded, cached lifecycle rules.

Scenarios.Scenario: Render and navigate the pinned-canvas sidebar and Back/Forward history
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Sidebar composition maps at most 5 pins into rows; nested observable updates patch row text/classes. Back/Forward resolves an in-memory history entry and shows an accepted custom-view state.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: At most 5 pin rows; recency history uses the existing bounded history structure.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: UI updates are synchronous observable reactions with no subprocess/network concurrency.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Rows retain pin objects and lazily create each hover toolbar. History rejects removed pin IDs rather than recreating unavailable views.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: changed render/update paths and history keys were inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None material due to the hard row cap.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: list work is bounded, toolbars are lazy, and pin state changes do not introduce collection-scale external calls.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass across all 46 changed files. Submitted one medium synchronous UI serialization finding. Subscription fan-out, cache/model retention, storage, cleanup, sidebar rendering, history, and agent-host boundaries were traced and otherwise found intentional, refcounted, or hard-capped.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
